questions.question: What are the key quality dimensions for evaluating software requirements?
choices: Length, font size, and color of the requirements document
Completeness, consistency, clarity, testability, and traceability
Number of requirements, file size, and page count
Which developer wrote them and when they were written
questions.explanation: High-quality requirements are complete (nothing missing), consistent (no contradictions), clear (unambiguous), testable (verifiable with concrete criteria), and traceable (linked to business goals and test cases).

questions.question: Why is 'testability' considered a critical quality dimension for requirements?
choices: Testability only matters for QA teams
Requirements that cannot be tested have no objective way to verify completion, leading to endless debates about whether the feature is 'done'
Testability is only relevant for unit tests
questions.explanation: If a requirement can't be tested, there's no objective way to confirm it's implemented correctly. This leads to ambiguity about 'done' status and disputes during acceptance. Testable requirements translate directly to acceptance criteria and test cases.

questions.question: How does an AI-powered requirements analyzer add value to the development process?
choices: It replaces the need for product managers entirely
It can automatically identify gaps, ambiguities, and inconsistencies in requirements before development begins, reducing costly rework
It generates the complete codebase from requirements
It only checks spelling and grammar
questions.explanation: AI-powered analysis can scan requirements for common quality issues — missing acceptance criteria, vague language, contradictory constraints, untested edge cases — catching problems early when they're far cheaper to fix.
